A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Distributed flexible job shop scheduling
Job priority
Memetic algorithm
Local search
A B S T R A C T
For the distributed flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP), the existing researches have predominantly
focused on operation sequence, machine selection and factory assignment, and assuming that the jobs have no
priority. However, in real-world manufacturing systems, production scheduling with job priority is very common
and is of concern to production managers. The paper presents a DFJSP with job priority (DFJSPJP) for the first
time, aiming at minimizing the makespan, total energy consumption and the weighted average time of jobs with
priority. A new memetic algorithm (NMA) is designed to solve the proposed DFJSPJP. In the proposed NMA, a
well-designed chromosome encoding method (CEM) is constructed to obtain a high-quality initial population. An
effective local search approach (LSO) is proposed to improve the NMA’s convergence speed and fully exploit its
solution space. Computational experiments conducted confirm the effectiveness of the CEM and LSO, and show
that the NMA is able to easily obtain better solutions for about 90 % of the tested 60 challenging problem in-
stances compared to other three well-known algorithms, demonstrating its superior performance on both solu-
tion quality and computational efficiency. This research will provide a theoretical basis for considering job
priority issues in distributed production environments and assist manufacturers in conducting accurate pro-
duction scheduling, thereby reducing resource waste and time loss caused by unreasonable production plans.

priority into account, in which there are a total of eight jobs and each job
has five operations. From Fig. 2, we can see that the makespan of these
two solutions is the same (equal to 80), and the completion times ofjobs

those in solution 2 are 72, 72, 68, 80, 62, 56, 48, 43, respectively.
According to the preferences of the production manager, the evalu
ation results of these two approaches may be completely different.
• If the production manager only cares about the completion time,
then the two solutions are the same; if the production manager only
cares about the priority ofjob 5, the two solutions are also the same.
• If the production manager is concerned about the priorities ofjobs 1,
2, and 3, solution 1 is better than solution 2.
• If the production manager is concerned about the priorities ofjobs 6,
7, and 8, then solution 2 is better than solution 1.

completion time and the priorities of jobs 1, 5, and 6, there is no
feasible solution.

algorithm to solve the DFJSPJP problem, in order to help production
managers make efficient decisions when considering problems with
different job priorities.
In this paper, a multi-objective DFJSPJP model is proposed, aiming
at minimizing the makespan, total energy consumption and the
weighted average time of jobs with priority. As far as we know, this is
the first time job priorities have been studied in related literature. MAs,
which integrate evolutionary algorithms with local search, have
demonstrated promising performance in solving multi-objective DFJSPs.
Motivated by this, we propose a new NMA to address the DFJSPJP we
proposed. In the NMA, a well-designed chromosome encoding mecha-
nism (CEM) is utilized to establish a high-quality initial population by
fully leveraging the information and structure of DFJSPJP. An effective
local search method (LSO) is proposed and integrated into the genetic
algorithm to enhance its convergence speed and fully exploit the solu-
tion space. Experimental results on a diverse set of up to 60 benchmark
instances from literature validate the effectiveness of the proposed NMA
and its components (CEM and LSO).

mathematical model of the proposed DFJSPJP. Section 4 details our
proposed NMA. Section 5 presents the experimental research and
discussion. Finally, conclusions are drawn in Section 6. The block dia-
gram of the entire research is shown in Fig. 3.
2. Literature review
2.1. DFJSP related work
De Giovanni and Pezzella [19] were pioneers in the study of DFJSP,
where tasks were allocated to multiple flexible manufacturing units fo
concurrent processing. They developed an enhanced genetic algorithm
(GA) incorporating greedy decoding and local search operators to tackle
this challenge. Subsequently, a plethora of researchers have devised
diverse approaches to address the DFJSP. Du et al. [20] set up a
constraint programming model and developed a hybrid algorithm tha
integrates a distribution estimation algorithm and variable neighbor
hood search (VNS) to tackle the DFJSP, aiming to minimize the make
span and crane transportation. Recognizing the decentralized nature of
the DFJSP model, Li et al. [21] introduced a hybrid tabu search algo
rithm with an optimization criterion and successfully applied it to a
practical DFJSP scenario. Marzouki et al. [22] opted for a multi-agent
system utilizing a meta-heuristic based on the forbidden search princi
ple to optimize job assignments and factory scheduling, achieving
commendable outcomes. Drawing inspiration from the collision princi
ple in chemical reactions, Marzouki et al. [23] innovatively proposed a
chemical reaction meta-heuristic algorithm for DFJSP optimization. Wu
and Liu [24] formulated a mixed integer linear model for DFJSP and
employed an enhanced differential evolutionary simulated annealing
algorithm to pursue locally optimal solutions. Jiang et al. [25] intro
duced an improved multi-objective decomposition evolutionary algo
rithm to optimize energy-efficient DFJSP, aiming to minimize makespan
and energy consumption. Chang and Liu [26] devised a hybrid GA
incorporating a roulette encoding method to address job assignment
challenges. Meng et al. [27] developed four mixed integer programming
models and an efficient constraint programming model to solve the
DFJSP, evaluating their efficacy through numerical experiments. They
designed an energy regulation strategy to enhance algorithm perfor
mance. Furthermore, various enhanced hybrid GAs have been widely
presented to tackle the complexities of DFJSP [28]. Wang et al. [18]
proposed an improved adaptive hybrid algorithm (IAHA) to tackle the
distributed flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP) in the contex
of economic globalization and distributed manufacturing. The algorithm
constructs a mathematical model for distributed factories, incorporate
a dual-level encoding hybrid decoding rule, and employs an adaptive
variable neighborhood search strategy to optimize cross-factory task
allocation. Experimental results show that IAHA breaks multiple record
and achieves optimal solutions in standard test cases involving 2 4
factories, highlighting its superior performance in solving DFJSP
compared to existing methods.

Gong et al. [29] made a breakthrough discovery that distributed
workshops encompass not only factories and machines, but also work-
shops that vary across different factories. Subsequently, they introduced
an effective memetic algorithm to tackle this challenge, aiming to

2.2. Work related to job priority
In today’s increasingly complex manufacturing environment, it is
inevitable to consider the priority of job processing. Processing high-
priority jobs as soon as possible will benefit the subsequent assembly
and transportation work in the entire factory. Production scheduling
with job priorities is very common and is a matter of great concern for
production managers. Therefore, many researchers have studied various
scheduling problems based on job priorities to achieve better production
scheduling solutions. Li et al. [35] proposed a highly efficient hybrid
self-adaptive differential evolution algorithm (HSDE) with heuristic
strategies. They studied the flexible job shop scheduling problem with
outsourcing and job priorities, achieving good results. Li et al. [36]
proposed a dual deep Q-network-based co-evolutionary algorithm
(D2QCE) to address the distributed heterogeneous hybrid flow shop
scheduling problem with multi-priority jobs (DHHFSP-MPJ). By
balancing global and local search, knowledge-driven neighborhood
structures, and energy-saving strategies, D2QCE significantly reduces
weighted tardiness and energy consumption. Experiments demonstrate
that D2QCE outperforms existing algorithms on 20 benchmark instances
and a real-world case of large-scale equipment manufacturing,
providing an efficient solution for engineering practices that consider
priority, delivery constraints, and resource optimization in scheduling
decisions.
From the above literature, it is evident that priority, as an important
research area in the academic community, has been highly valued by
many researchers. However, previous studies on distributed flexible job
shops did not consider the issue ofjob priorities, which is actually one of
the most common requirements in modern production scenarios. For
example, in a batch of job orders, there are several jobs that need to be
manufactured with priority. How should we handle such orders?
Therefore, this paper innovatively studied the DFJSP considering job
priorities, not only opening up a new research branch theoretically for
future researchers, but also providing practical solutions for producers
facing the DFJSP situations with job priority requirements.

5. Experiments and analysis
The proposed NMA for the DFJSPJP was executed in MATLAB
R2020a and run on a computer with an Intel Core i5 2.9 GHz and 16 GB
RAM. To test the performance of NMA, three experiments were carried
out. Firstly, the key parameters of four algorithms, including NMA, were
determined through Taguchi experiments [46,47], and NMA was
compared with the other three algorithms. Then, verify the validity of
the operators proposed in this paper. Finally, the superior performance
of NMA algorithm is proved by comparing with other algorithms. Each
benchmark instance was run 10 times to reduce randomness in the
experimental results.
5.1. Constructing the DFSPJP benchmarks
In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed NMA in dealing
with the DFJSPJP model, a set of 60 DFJSPJP benchmark instances
(named DDs 01–60) were created based on established examples of the
traditional DFJSPJP standard. These instances are categorized into three
sizes: small benchmark instances (DDs 01–20), medium benchmark in-
stances (DDs 21 40), and large benchmark instances (DDs 41 60). In all
the instances developed, the machine’s power consumption of each
processing unit time is randomly set between 5 and 15; the unit trans-
port time between different factories, workshops, and machines are
defined as 20, 10, and
respectively; the unit energy consumption
resulting from unit transportation time is set to 10. The generated
benchmark instances DDs 01–60 are available for download from the
following website: https://github.com/Heao1234/Heao.

5.3. Parameter settings
Different parameters affect the overall performance of the algorithm,
so it is necessary to tune the settings of the key parameters. In this paper,
the key parameters include population size (NP), crossover probability
(CP), mutation probability (MP), and local search probability (LP). Here,
the Taguchi experimental method is employed to calibrate the level of
each key parameter in NMA and the three competitive algorithms.
Specifically, we designed an orthogonal experiment containing 16
parameter combinations, as shown in columns 2–5 of Table 4. The four
levels for each parameter are set as follows: NP = [60,90,120,150], CP =
0.30, 0.40, 0.50]. Three instances were selected for the experiment
including small-scale (DD01), medium-scale (DD 32) and large-scale
(DD 54), and the IGD was selected as the evaluation index for the
experimental results.
5.3.2. Parameter calibration of the comparison algorithms
In this paper, NNIA [53], NSGA-II [54], and NSGA-III [5,55] were
selected as comparison algorithms. The main reasons for choosing these
three comparison algorithms are as follows: (1) all of the NNIA, NSGA-II,
NSGA-III, and NMA are based on traditional genetic algorithms, so they
have similar frameworks; (2) all these algorithms use the non-dominated
sorting method to deal with multi-objective problems; and (3) all these
algorithms are classical algorithms are usually used as the baseline al-
gorithms to verify the effectiveness of the newly proposed
multi-objective algorithms.
To ensure the fairness of the experiment, the Taguchi experiment is

6. Conclusion and future research
In this paper, we studied the DFJSPJP considering the completion
time, total energy consumption, and the weighted average time of job
priorities. The DFJSPJP can assist production managers in dealing with
scheduling issues involving job priorities, which are widespread in the
real world but have been completely neglected in theoretical research.
We propose an effective NMA to solve the DFJSPJP. In the NMA, an CEM
was constructed by sufficiently making use of the information and
structure of the DFJSPJP, which can guarantee the NMA to obtain a
high-quality initial population; and a local search operator (LSO) with
two methods is designed to enhance the convergence speed of the NMA.

In the experimental section, we first construct 60 benchmark in
stances based on some classic FJSP benchmark instances to test the al-
gorithm’s performance. Fairly, the critical parameters of the NMA and
the other three comparative algorithms (NNIA, NSGA-II, and NSGA-III)
are calibrated using the Taguchi method. Additionally, we select 60
large, medium, and small-scale instances to validate the effectiveness of
the proposed LSO. Furthermore, extensive comparisons between our
proposed NMA and three well-known algorithms are conducted based
on the 60 constructed benchmark instances. From these experimental
results, it is evident that the NMA, evaluated based on C-metric, IGD,
and HV evaluation metrics, outperforms the other three comparative
algorithms significantly
Our research provides significant social value in both theoretical and
practical aspects. From a theoretical perspective, this study proposes a
novel research direction for DFJSP by first incorporating job priority in
distributed production environments. Furthermore, the proposed NMA
algorithm and benchmark instances can serve as a reference for other
researchers to design multi-objective optimization algorithms with local
search operators and to test their algorithms using our benchmark in-
stances. From the practical point of view, our proposed DFJSPJP model
can effectively distribute the production of high-priority jobs. As a
result, companies can improve productivity by ensuring that critical
orders are delivered on time without compromising the overall
schedule. In addition, the resulting scheduling scheme helps to addres
the problem of workers working overtime to meet deadlines, thereby
reducing worker overload and the safety accidents it may cause.
In the future work, some advanced algorithms can be introduced to
enhance the performance of the algorithm, such as the latest meta-
heuristic algorithms (e.g., flying fox optimizer) and reinforcement
learning. Furthermore, the shop scheduling problem with job priority
can be extend to dynamic scheduling scenarios (e.g., considering ma-
chine failures with planned outages).
